the final part where everything is explained

questions.q: Write a PETZAAL paragraph on the key line (Point, Evidence, Zoom in, Analyse).
questions.a: For example: 'rarer' suggests forgiveness is less common and so more precious than revenge.

questions.q: Name one character whose ending is not fully happy, and why.
questions.a: Antonio (no remorse), or Caliban (still a servant, though he seeks grace).

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a PETZAAL paragraph: 'How does Shakespeare present forgiveness at the end of The Tempest?' Starter: 'At the end of the play, Shakespeare presents forgiveness as...'
questions.a: A PETZAAL paragraph on the key line, Ariel's influence or Prospero's giving up of magic, with an Alternative on Antonio.

questions.q: Extend: what does 'I'll drown my book' suggest?
questions.a: Prospero gives up magic and control, returning to ordinary human life and responsibility.

questions.q: Stretch: is the ending a true resolution? Judge in one sentence.
questions.a: Mostly: the families are joined and Ariel is free, but Antonio's silence leaves a question.

options: It leaves doubt about whether he has changed
questions.a: C) It leaves doubt about whether he has changed. Antonio never apologises, so forgiveness here is one-sided; A and B are not in the text.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: what would you do, and what does Prospero's choice teach?
questions.a: Answers vary; Prospero teaches that mercy shown from strength breaks the cycle of revenge.
